findings.title: Punks winding up 46-55° off the look at strike range are off-screen and unwarned
findings.detail: SPEC §8 fires the warning when 'an enemy the player can't see starts winding up' (more than 55° from camera forward), and SPEC §5 sets the field of view at 90° horizontal (first_person_camera.gd:102 keep_aspect = KEEP_WIDTH, fov_deg 90, so the view edge is at ±45°). Part B §B1 measures the bearing from the player's origin (player.gd:194-195 look_bearing_deg, then ViewGeometry). The lens sits ahead of the origin (the throat lens plus cam_forward_offset_m), so at the Punk's strike distance (0.9-1.0 m) the Punk is about 9-10° further round as seen from the lens than the rule thinks. I measured frozen real Punks at 0.95 m in the crowd room. At 40° and 45° (origin bearing) only the near fist is in the camera frustum: an arm at the left edge, with the head and chest off-screen. At 50° and 54° none of origin, chest, head or fists is in the frustum (a red sleeve sliver at the left edge), and no warning. At 56° and 60° there is likewise nothing in the frustum, and the warning lights. On the right side, -50° shows a bit more (head and arm at the edge). So a band of about 46-55° per side is effectively blind and unwarned. In the crowd, 5 of 134 wind-ups started in that band, and 4 of them landed jab plus cross unblocked with no corner lit. R10 cannot see this: the oracle builds its expected corner from the same ViewGeometry rule from the same origin, so it agrees by construction. The done-when's behind-left, behind-right and behind clauses are unaffected; SPEC §8's purpose (warn of what the player can't see) is not met in this band.

findings.suggested_fix: Preferred, since the gate is locking feel defaults: measure the rule's bearing from the lens, not the body origin. Have PlayerCharacter.look_bearing_deg() and is_outside_view() pass a point a tunable distance ahead along the flat look (or the rig's eye point, which AudioDirector's listener already uses) as `from` to ViewGeometry. This stays simulation-safe and matches SPEC's 'from camera forward' more closely. The director's blind spot follows automatically, and test_view_geometry is unchanged (the function is pure). It needs Part B §B1's 'measured from the player's origin' amended, and the in-view negative control (warning_bot 'Warn: in view' and B3) moved from 50° to about 40° at 0.9 m. Alternative: retune rear_warning_angle_deg from 55 to about 46-47. That changes a SPEC §8 number and would have to be logged as a departure taken by default. Either way, add a crowd-room test: a Punk at 50° and 0.95 m whose chest is outside the FP frustum must warn.

findings.title: Warning re-arms at revive while the KO view is still on screen (training room)
findings.detail: RearWarning suppresses only while the player's health is 0 (rear_warning.gd:277-281 _suppressed; Part B §B1.9). But _revive() restores health at once (player.gd:663-664) while the KO view eases back to the eyes over ko_view_in_s 0.5 s (first_person_camera.gd:305-316), and look_yaw is reset to the body's facing. A wind-up that starts in that window lights a corner over the third-person shot of the player getting up. In the review bot, the revive is at f802; a dummy at the pre-KO +135° winds up at f807, and both corners light while the frame still shows the lying or rising body from outside. In the crowd room this can't happen: the director holds wind-ups for director_revive_grace_s 1.5 s, longer than the 0.5 s return. In the training room it can: one dummy spars by default (test_room.gd sparring_dummies [1], F5 for all). The L1 lens asks for the hide during the KO view, not only at health 0.
findings.evidence: captures/review/rbot/bot.log: 'REVIVED Player f802', 'W+ side=left count=1 heavy=false f807', 'W+ side=right count=1 heavy=false f807', 'WU+ Dummy2 f807', '  getup f808 L(a=0.84 s=1.19 n=1) R(a=0.84 s=1.19 n=1) hp=100'. Sheet captures/review/sheets/r_ko_full.png, row 5 col 3 (video frame 808): the third-person KO view of the player rising, with both bursts lit.
findings.repro: cd /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m3-review-slice-warn && tools/capture_bot.sh res://tests/bot/review_warn_bot.tscn captures/review/rbot "Rev: KO view" (god mode off, 5 HP, a jab KOs the player; after the auto-revive a dummy behind winds up within 0.5 s).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the warning suppressed until the view is back in the eyes. Either keep it hidden for ko_view_in_s after CombatEvents.revived (a presentation-side timer on the revived event), or while the player is in the get-up that follows a KO (read the state; the HUD writes nothing). Word Part B §B1.9 as 'the KO view, until it is back in the eyes'. Add a case to test_it_hides_while_the_player_is_ko.

crowd.summary:
Lens L2 (first-person crowd readability) on the slice at 356fccf. I recorded acts 1-4 and Waves myself; they match the builder's headless_final run exactly. I also recorded an extra crowd-knockdown act, ran 15 headless act runs with a per-enemy lens-attribution probe, and made three windowed R15 runs.

Hard metrics: all pass in 42 act runs (R1 max 2, R2 min 21 f, R3 0 unwarned, R10 100% with 0 false positives, R11 0). Also passing: flinch-lock (longest chain 0.72-1.13 s, under 1.5 s), stalls (R13 0 stuck everywhere), R15 (p95 12.2-12.3 ms, spawn hitch 26-31.5 ms). In-lens wind-ups read at 1 m. Taunts and strafes don't read as threats.

The L2 rubric is not all yes:
- Q6 fails: more than half the view is covered by enemies outside an attack, e.g. 60.75-61.25 s in Six Punks, observed.
- Q5 only partly holds: a wall of Punks forms at strike range, and only 0.5-2.1 of six Punks are posturing at any time.
- Q1 and Q10 fail for about 7% of wind-ups: those start 45-55 degrees off the look, outside the 90-degree lens but inside the warning's 55 degrees, so only an arm shows and no warning fires.

Root causes found:
1. A real mechanical bug in EnemyActor. The latched avoidance velocity goes stale through the attack and the RECOVER hold, so a Punk backing off can walk the wrong way, sometimes at 4-6 m/s. One back-off circled 342 degrees round the player at 0.76-1.1 m. A two-line local patch (not committed) cut wrong-way frames by 85-95%, with every hard metric still passing.
2. 73-86% of the over-half lens coverage (R8 misses, p95 50-62%) comes from Punks that are not attacking: the RECOVER hold, a token holder waiting at strike range, a Punk walking back after a hit. A Punk winding up alone covers only p50 34% of the lens.
3. Attack cadence is the cheapest lever. At punk_attack_cooldown_s 6, two to three of the six Punks are posturing at a time, the passive player lasts 15-17 s instead of 12-14 s, and R8 drops (Six Punks, observed p95 61% to 34%). The cost is about 30-40% fewer wind-ups.

All recordings and scratch probes are in /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m3-review-slice-crowd/captures/review and tests/review_scratch/. Nothing was committed.

Blind-spot priority 1.0 (SPEC literal) means 65-75% of six-Punk wind-ups start outside the view. WARN-CHECK counts in my fight recording: 24 warned of 33. The Punks in front mostly stand while the ones behind attack, so readability leans on the corner bursts. This follows the spec; it is a feel default to lock knowingly.

'Six Punks, fight' can't show the attack-recover cycle. Only 1 of 31 wind-ups reached ATTACK; 28 went WINDUP->REACT (blocked on the first active frame, or punched out), and CROWD reports 0.0 backing off. Rubric Q7 has to be judged from observed and passive.

The builder's recordings in .worktrees/m3-p1-int/captures/p1-int were made before 8020ad4, so some numbers differ from the final code (observed: 27 vs 25 hits, ring median 3.16 vs 3.40). Quote headless_final or my acts14 numbers in M3-slice-gate.md.

A token holder at strike range waits with no timeout of its own (enemy_actor.gd:599-610 only counts frames while still closing). Only the director's 4 s token timeout applies.
RoomKit.PlayerObstacle (room_kit.gd:22-45) never sets its velocity, so the avoidance treats a player being knocked back at 3.5 m/s as standing still.

findings.title: Backing-off Punks walk the wrong way at up to 6 m/s because the latched avoidance velocity is stale
findings.evidence:
Frame trace (captures/review/cov3_bot.log, Six Punks observed, seed 0):
- f480-f502, ATTACK then the RECOVER hold: navvel=(0.00,0.00) and simvel=(0,0), but safe stays at (2.44,3.34) to (2.38,3.31).
- f504, first walking tick: navvel=(-1.73,-1.94), toward the slot; simvel=(2.38,3.31), the opposite way.
- f504-f516: simvel stays about (2.6,3.6) while the Punk crosses past the player from (0.07,-1.17) to (0.59,-0.47).
Result in cov2/bot.log: Punk5's back-off from f485 lasts 5.58 s and sweeps 342 degrees around the player, 3.25 s of it within 1.3 m, though its slot was only 28 degrees away at the start. In my recording this is observed 60.25-61.25 s: observed_orbit_4fps_59.png frames 5-9, two Punks side by side covering 85-90% of the lens.
Frequency, ww0-2 (3 seeds, 5 acts):
- moving more than 90 degrees off the wanted direction: 0.1-7.0% of walking frames;
- episodes up to 62 frames, applied speed up to 6.0 m/s (ww0 observed Punk3 f2916-2977; ww2 fight Punk18 f4783-4843 at 4.2 m/s toward the player);
- back-offs sweeping more than 90 degrees: up to 4 per act, max 342 and 291 degrees.
Two-line local patch in _stop() (_safe_velocity = Vector3.ZERO; _nav.set_velocity_forced(Vector3.ZERO)), wwA0 and wwA2:
- wrong-way frames 105 to 18 (observed s0), 104 to 5 (fight s0), 167 to 17 (fight s2); longest episode 62 to 8 f;
- max orbit 342 to 194 degrees; hard rows ok in all 10 acts.
enemy_max_speed_mps 3.0 alone removes the speeds above 3 m/s but not the wrong direction (wwt0: Punk5 still 60 f toward the player).
findings.repro: cd .worktrees/m3-review-slice-crowd && godot --headless --path . --fixed-fps 60 res://tests/review_scratch/review_bot.tscn -- "--act=Six Punks, observed" --probe-out=captures/review/x --trace=Punk5:480:560, then read the TRACE lines (simvel vs navvel at f504). Or watch acts14/bot.avi at 58.5-62 s.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. In EnemyActor, clear the latch whenever the body stops or a move takes over: in _stop() and _stop_reporting(), set _safe_velocity = Vector3.ZERO and call _nav.set_velocity_forced(Vector3.ZERO). Do the same when RECOVER and the REACT-to-APPROACH change begin.
2. In _apply_velocity(), never apply a safe velocity more than 90 degrees off the desired one (use zero that tick), and clamp its length to the desired speed.
3. Re-run test_slice_crowd and the determinism test.
The remaining long back-offs (P1-int call 17: a path blocked by a waiting Punk) still need the slot or back-off decision that call asks for.

findings.title: 7% of wind-ups start 45-55 degrees off the look: outside the 90-degree lens, inside the warning's 55 degrees
findings.detail: With the default 90-degree horizontal FOV the lens edge is at 45 degrees, but the warning (SPEC §8: 'more than 55 degrees from camera forward') only fires beyond 55. A Punk winding up at 1 m inside that band shows only a shoulder and one hand at the screen edge, so its pose can't be read and no corner lights. The shove's two-palm wind-up, its distinguishing tell, is invisible. This fails rubric Q1 ('see the wind-up pose for most of its length') and Q10 ('know why they took damage') for those hits. At the minimum FOV of 75 degrees the blind band grows to 37.5-55 degrees.
findings.evidence:
Wind-up start bearings over 357 wind-ups (ww0-2, every act): 26 at 45-55 degrees, 19 at 35-45, 87 under 35, 225 beyond 55 (warned).
observed_edge_shove_12fps.png (acts14 at 54.1-54.52 s): Punk2's shove (WU+ f3256, strike f3276, 'WARN-CHECK ok ... none f3256') shows only a red shoulder and one palm at the left edge; no head, no two-palm silhouette, no corner burst. Then the palm sweeps into the lens.
The same event at 54.3-54.47 s in observed_6fps_1.png frames 1-2.
findings.repro: View acts14/bot.avi at 54.1-54.7 s, or count wind-ups with 45 < |look_bearing_deg| <= 55 at WU+ in any six-Punk act.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask Game-boy, since 55 degrees is SPEC §8's number. Option A: derive the threshold from the lens, e.g. fov_deg / 2 plus a small margin, so 'can't see it' and 'warned' meet. Option B: keep 55 for the warning, but have the director treat 45-55 degrees as blind for posture slots, so Punks don't attack from the band. Either way, record it in README's M3 departures.

findings.title: R5 (front-wedge crowding) can't see the wall that forms
findings.detail: R5 counts only enemies in AiState.POSTURE (P1-instruments call 21). But the front crowd is made of token holders waiting at strike range (ENGAGE), the RECOVER hold, and walk-backs. So R5 reads 0.0% in every act while the sheets show two Punks side by side filling the front. The gate cites R5 for rubric Q5, so it gives false comfort.
findings.evidence: R5 '0.0% of frames' in all 42 act runs (acts14, waves, ww0-2, cov, kd), while observed_orbit_4fps_59.png frames 7-9 (60.75-61.25 s) show two Punks within 1.1 m in the front wedge. In my COV samples, frames with 2 or more Punks within 1.3 m and |bearing| under 50 degrees run 4.5-9.4% in observed and fight (cov/bot.log). readability_probe.gd:420-430 filters on _is_posturing().
findings.repro: Run any six-Punk act with the probe and compare R5 with the CROWD line's '... waiting at strike range, ... still within it in RECOVER' or with the sheets.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a companion row, or redefine R5: share of frames with 2 or more standing, non-attacking enemies (any AiState except WINDUP, ATTACK and KO, actor state not DOWNED or LAUNCHED) within ±45 degrees and within 1.5 m. Keep the posture-only count as R5a if the plan wants it.

code.summary: L4 (code and layers) review of the M3 slice diff (c971cf4..356fccf), done in /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m3-review-slice-code. The game code holds up. Nothing in the simulation reads a camera, the presentation layer writes no game state, and every timing, distance, chance and speed comes from Tuning or move data. Tokens are released on every exit path I traced, F6 included. The navigation agent uses the latched velocity pattern, enemies leave their groups before they are freed, and the director's clock is correct at 1x and at the 0.25x cheat. Determinism and test flakiness are clean: two full suites gave 866/866 with 0 ERROR lines each. test_slice_crowd and test_enemy_director give identical output in separate processes, and the same crowd-bot act with the same seed is identical across processes. All hard metrics pass in every P1-int readability.json: R1 ≤ 3 (the cap), R2 ≥ 21 frames, R3 0, R10 100% with 0 false positives, R11 0. I changed no feel defaults. Every scratch file is deleted, the worktree's git status is clean, nothing was committed and no Godot process is left running.

findings.title: Per-act readability numbers can't be reproduced: R4 and R8 sample on the absolute frame, and acts carry state from the act run before
findings.detail: The probe takes its occlusion (R4) and lens-coverage (R8) samples when Engine.get_physics_frames() % occlusion_every (or % lens_every) == 0. Which frames of an act get sampled therefore depends on everything that ran before it. Identical simulations then give different soft numbers. Separately, the crowd bot's acts are not independent of the act before them, although P1-int call 10 says 'an act's numbers do not depend on which acts ran before it'. Per-frame metrics move too (R6 and the CROWD meter), so the simulation itself differs, not only the sampling. The gate quotes readability.json from runs of different make-up (single-act directories, headless_all, h_rest), so small differences between sources are expected and are not regressions. Hard metrics are unaffected.
findings.evidence: readability_probe.gd:342 and 353-356 (frame % occlusion_every, frame % lens_every on the absolute frame). full_run1.log vs full_run2.log: the six-Punk WARN-CHECK frames are all shifted by exactly 4, yet R8 p50 reads 10% vs 9%, and the autopilot act reads R4 '0% of 3' vs '0% of 1' and R8 p50 8% vs 6%. 'Six Punks, blind spot' alone (bot_blind_1.log) or after 'Six Punks, passive' (bot_passive_blind.log): R6 median 3.16 m, R8 p50 15%, CROWD '1.1 backing off, 0.44 still within it in RECOVER'. After 'Three Punks' (bot_three_blind.log): R6 3.11 m, R8 p50 16%, CROWD '1.0 backing off, 0.43'.
findings.repro: cd the review worktree; godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after 40000 --path . res://tests/bot/crowd_bot.tscn -- "--act=Three Punks|Six Punks, blind spot" and compare the blind spot act's R6, R8 and CROWD lines with a run of --act="Six Punks, blind spot" alone. For the phase effect, run tools/run_tests.sh twice and diff the R4 and R8 lines of test_slice_crowd.
findings.suggested_fix: Sample on (frame - _start_frame) % n in ReadabilityProbe.tick(). In crowd_bot._reset(), also reset what carries between acts, then confirm by rerunning the pair above: TimeController.clear(), the spawner's RNG, and the director's clock, reslot timer and _last_* times (e.g. a test-only EnemyDirector.reset()). Or say in the gate file that soft metrics vary by about ±1-2 points between run compositions.

findings.title: A director made by EnemyDirector.ensure() (F4 spawns in the training room) is never seeded
findings.detail: rng_seed is only applied through its property setter, so a director that is never assigned a seed keeps RandomNumberGenerator.new()'s default. In Godot 4.7 that default is randomized. CrowdRoom assigns the seed, but EnemyDirector.ensure() (the training-room F4 path and the S0 fallback) does not. The blind-spot priority roll is then not reproducible from run to run whenever blind_spot_priority is below 1.0. That contradicts the class doc ('Seeds the director's random rolls') and the 2.6 contract ('seeded RNG').
findings.evidence: enemy_director.gd:33-36 (seed applied in the setter only), :46 (_rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()), :128-135 (ensure() sets no seed). Scratch run: two fresh EnemyDirectors had RNG seeds 7849026454339830248 and -138142339259082094 (captures/review/review_code.log:18). Two fresh RNGs had different first randf values, 0.939588 vs 0.102315 (:17).
findings.repro: In the training room, set blind_spot_priority to 0.5 in F1, F4-spawn three Punks around the player, and log the TOK+ order. Restart and repeat: the grant order differs between runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the seed unconditionally in _init() or _ready() (_rng.seed = rng_seed), so the default 0 actually seeds.

findings.title: The 'resources still in use at exit' fix lives only in the bots: a headless fixed-fps run of the main scene still prints it
findings.detail: P1-int's fix (stop every player, wait about 150-250 ms of real time, then quit) is in crowd_bot._quit() and test_slice_crowd.after_all() only. The game itself does not drain its audio on quit. Any other headless, fixed-fps harness of the crowd room that ends during a fight therefore prints an ERROR line plus a leak WARNING, all of them audio streams and playbacks. Examples are a new bot, a smoke run or a check_m3_log.py input. Windowed play and a real-time headless 900-frame run were clean, so Game-boy will not see it. But A7.4's release smoke greps for ERROR, and run with --fixed-fps it would fail on this. That would need the same explanation every time.
findings.evidence: captures/review/main_headless.log: 'WARNING: 41 ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit' and 'ERROR: 13 resources still in use at exit' from godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after 1500 --path . The --verbose run (main_headless_verbose.log:394-451) lists only AudioStreamWAV (effort, whoosh, thud, player_grunt) and AudioStreamPlaybackWAV. Clean: training room, same flags (training_headless.log); windowed 1500 frames (main_windowed.log); headless without fixed fps, 900 frames (main_headless_nofixed.log).
findings.repro: cd the review worktree && godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after 1500 --path . 2>&1 | grep -E 'ERROR|leaked'
findings.suggested_fix: Give AudioDirector a quit drain: on NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST, or a GameInput quit hook, stop all voices and wait a short real-time delay before quitting, and drop the bot-side copies. At minimum, note in HANDOFF and A7.4 that headless smoke runs must not use --fixed-fps.

findings.title: A few public members of the new room code have no ## doc comment
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md requires ## doc comments on public API. RoomKit.box_mesh() and RoomKit.flat_material() are public static helpers with none. CrowdRoom's room-contract members player, spawner, director, geometry and nav_region (the 2.12 contract that bots and tests use) have none either, while nav_bake_usec beside them does. Everything else in the M3 game diff is documented.
findings.evidence: game/level/room_kit.gd:107 (static func box_mesh) and :116 (static func flat_material). game/level/crowd_room.gd:105-109 (var player, spawner, director, geometry, nav_region).
findings.repro: Read the lines above. An awk pass over the M3 files for public functions not preceded by ## found only these two new ones; the other hits are pre-M3.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one-line ## docs to those two functions and five variables.
